elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as rendered: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other", with the new proviso restricting only HDI to term-end effectiveness, so the Company retains a no-cause exit specifying its own Termination Date.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The retained notice period is "ninety (90) days written notice"; no 30-day Company notice right was inserted.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere in the rendered text; Section 4.2 only imposes a payment running from Company to HDI.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: New proviso: "provided that termination by HDI shall be effective only at the end of the then-current term" expressly ties HDI's effective date to term end, so HDI cannot exit mid-term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated" — a mutual no-cause exit on 90 days' notice, within the 60–90 day band; the added proviso confines the term-end limitation to HDI only, leaving the Company's right unrestricted. (The deterministic "Customer convenience termination present" flag is false because the drafting uses "terminated by either Party" rather than the words "for convenience"/"without cause"; in substance a no-cause right exists.)

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The insertion reads "provided that the Termination Payment shall not exceed three (3) months of fees", but no "Fees" term appears in the resolved definitions and the consideration/Termination Payment mechanics in this hosting agreement are expressed in "Net Sales" (aggregate Net Sales for twelve months less $800,000, divided by two). The cap therefore rests on an undefined and possibly non-existent measure, so its quantum is indeterminate.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: "provided that termination by HDI shall be effective only at the end of the then-current term" — the termination effective date is expressly tied to term end, satisfying the boundary rule that an auto-renewal notice right alone is insufficient.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Retained "ninety (90) days written notice" applies to "either Party", including HDI.

reasons: Fallback is not position-complete: the early-termination fee cap is expressed as "three (3) months of fees", but this agreement quantifies HDI's economics in "Net Sales" and no defined "Fees" exists in the resolved definitions. Repair by anchoring the cap to a defined amount actually payable under the agreement (e.g., "shall not exceed an amount equal to three (3) (months') average Net Sales-based amounts payable to HDI under Section [x] for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date"), or by defining "fees" in the operative text.

The same undefined measure is why intent is not preserved: the inserted proviso leaves a dangling monetary reference inside a formula otherwise driven by Net Sales and $800,000, creating an indeterminate (and arguably inoperative) cap alongside the retained 4.2(b) zero-floor and 4.2(c) eight-instalment mechanics.

Vendor-side elements are properly fixed: the HDI proviso expressly ties the effective date to the end of the then-current term, and the retained 90-day mutual notice satisfies the Vendor notice floor.

Customer-side notice sits at the fallback band (90 days) rather than the preferred 30 days, and no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund was added, so the preferred level is not reached — acceptable if the fallback is completed.

Minimality is satisfied: only two targeted provisos were added, each mapped to a fallback element; the 4.2(b)/(c) mechanics, the Net Sales formula and the mutual notice period were all retained without cosmetic deletions.
Severity remains high pending repair: as rendered, the Company's exit still carries a Termination Payment whose ceiling is unascertainable.
